figures.caption: Figure 1: Number of type 1 equilibria (N1) and number of asymptotically stable type 1 equilibria (S1) in the delay-free case (see Proposition 4.2) in the regions of the (κ, η) parameter plane delimited by the saddle-node curve Γ (1) SN (dashed) and the boundary line Σ (horizontal axis).
Figure 2: (left) First critical delay τ (1)0 in the discrete-delay case and (right) the corresponding first Lyapunov coefficient ℓ1 evaluated at τ = τ (1)

Figure 3: Number (N2) and classification of type 2 equilibria in the delay-free case (see Proposition 5.2) in the regions of the (κ, η) parameter plane delimited by the saddle-node curve Γ (2) SN (dashed) and the boundary line η = 0.
Figure 4: (left) First critical delay τ (2)1 in the discrete-delay case and (right) the corresponding first Lyapunov coefficient ℓ1 evaluated at τ = τ (2)
Figure 5: Stability scenarios of the type 2 delay-free center z⋆c when a discrete Dirac kernel with delay τ is considered in the system.

Figure 6: Attractor classification for selected values of the discrete delay τ . Region labels denote (S1, S2, C), with S1 the number of stable type 1 equilibria, S2 the number of stable type 2 equilibria, and C the number of stable cycles arising from the first Hopf branches. Gray regions indicate parameter values for which the present local bifurcation-based classification detects no stable attractor among the tracked branches. The numbered points denote the parameter sets found in Table 1 and used in the numerical simulations.
Table 1: Parameter values and delay values used in the numerical simulations.

Figure 7: Set 1: (top) Regions of attraction and (bottom) trajectories for (κ, η) = (4.0, 0.92). The trajectories are shown for all types of behavior of interest: (top) limit cycles; (middle) type 2 equilibria; and (bottom) type 1 equilibria.
Figure 8: Set 2: Phase portraits for (κ, η) = (−0.1, 0.9).

Figure 9: Regions of attraction and representative trajectories for the two third-quadrant parameter sets. In each panel, the upper image shows the regions of attraction and the lower image shows representative trajectories.

Figure 10: Set 4: (top) Regions of attraction and (bottom) trajectories for (κ, η) = (3,−0.4). The trajectories are shown for all types of behavior of interest: (top) limit cycles; (middle) type 2 equilibria; and (bottom) type 1 equilibria.
